2604.21732 A key ingredient to fully unlock the potential of Ge heterostructures for coherent spin physics is their intrinsic Rashba spin–orbit interaction (SOI) [ 1 , 34 , 35 , 36 ] , which provides direct electrical control of the spin state [ 37 , 38 , 7 , 39 , 40 , 5 , 41 , 42 , 43 , 44 , 45 , 8 , 46 , 6 , 47 , 48 , 49 ] , and enables tuneable spin response in quantum dots [ 50 , 51 ] , potentially compensating for disorder and variability that fundamentally limits large-scale integration [ 52 , 53 , 54 , 55 ] . In hybrid superconducting-semiconducting architectures, large intrinsic SOI ensures strong coupling to superconducting resonators [ 56 , 57 , 58 , 59 ] , efficient manipulation of superconducting (Andreev) spin qubits [ 60 , 61 , 62 , 63 ] , and topological phases of matter [ 64 , 65 , 66 , 67 , 68 , 69 , 70 , 71 , 72 , 15 , 73 , 74 ] . Yet, state-of-the-art Ge heterostructures, based on compressively-strained channels ( ε \varepsilon -Ge) sandwiched by strain-relaxed silicon-germanium (SiGe) barriers, show negligible intrinsic SOI due to large epitaxial strain fields, posing challenges for efficient spin manipulation.
